title: The web app has no CI job, so its tests never run
description:
**Found 2026-09-16 while reviewing a delegated web change.**

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` defines exactly two jobs: `python` and `infra`. The string `web` appears in it **zero times**.

So the web app has **no CI gate at all** — not tests, not lint, not typecheck. `web/package.json` defines all three scripts and nothing runs them.

## Why this matters now

- `web/lib/*.test.ts` currently holds **64 passing tests** that no pipeline executes. They protect the turn-grant payload builder, which is the code path deciding what authority a bot receives.
- [PR #353](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/pull/353) is a web-only change to exactly that code. **CI will pass it without running a single web test.**
- Two web changes merged in the last week (#351 assistant-ui spike, #346 the real workspace) were likewise ungated.

A test suite nobody runs is worse than no suite: it reads as coverage in review and catches nothing.

## What to build

A third job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, modelled on the existing `infra` job (lines 55-76) — same `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: "22"`, `cache: npm`, `cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json`, and `npm ci` at the root, since this is an npm workspace.

Then, with `working-directory: web`:

1. `npm test`
2. `npm run lint`
3. `npm run typecheck`

## Expect typecheck to be the interesting one

`npm run typecheck` may fail on first run. **If it does, report the errors — do not delete the step, do not add `continue-on-error`, and do not weaken `tsconfig`.** A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. If the errors are real, they become a separate card and this one lands with the two steps that do pass, plus a note.

Do not "fix" type errors by casting to `any` or adding `@ts-ignore`.

## Constraints

- Do not change `web/package.json` scripts.
- Do not touch the `python` or `infra` jobs.
- Do not change any application code. This card is CI configuration only.
- Keep the job independent of the others so a web failure does not mask a python failure.

## Verification

Push the branch and read the actual run. **Do not report success from reading YAML** — this project has repeatedly found things that were green at one layer and broken at a seam. The evidence is a run URL and its job results.

## Done when

A `web` job appears in CI, runs on the same triggers as the others, executes the suite, and demonstrably fails when a web test fails. Prove that last part deliberately if it is cheap to do so.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Review: ACCEPTED — [PR #354](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/pull/354) (2026-09-16)

Implemented by a delegated Haiku sub-agent. The agent wrote and locally verified; the push, PR and real-run evidence were mine, because CI triggers only on pushes to `main`/`develop` and on pull requests, so a branch push alone produces no run.

### Verified independently

| Claim | How checked | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Three gates pass | Re-ran all three myself | `npm test` 60 pass 0 fail, lint clean, **typecheck 0 errors** |
| YAML valid and wired | `yaml.safe_load`, inspected job keys | jobs are `python`, `infra`, `web`; steps are checkout, setup-node, Install, Test, Lint, Typecheck |
| Scope | `git status` | Only `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No app code, no `package.json`, no other job |
| No `continue-on-error`, no weakened config | Read the diff | None present |
| **The gate can actually fail** | Broke an assertion, checked the exit code | **`npm test` exits 1.** Restored afterwards |
| Real CI run | [PR #354](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/pull/354) | **`web` job passes in 35s**; `infra` passes; `python` still running |

The exit-code check is the one that mattered. A runner that prints failures but exits 0 would produce a permanently green step — worse than the gap, because it would look like coverage.

### The agent's test count was right and mine was wrong to compare against

It reported 60 tests where I had measured 64. That is consistent: the 4 extra are the revoke tests on `feat/b7e2c7-revoke-turn-authority`, not on `develop`.

### Correction to this card's premise

This card said to expect typecheck to fail and to leave the step out if so. **It passes.** My earlier report of failures on `develop` was a stale local `node_modules` — `@assistant-ui/react` is declared in `web/package.json`, and after `npm ci` typecheck is clean. The agent ran `npm ci` first, as instructed, and found the truth. The step is included.

### Outstanding

Job logs are not retrievable until the whole run completes, and `python` is still going. **35s is fast enough that the log deserves reading** to confirm the steps really executed rather than no-opping. Not treating this as fully closed until that is checked.

comments.text:
## Log verification complete — outstanding item closed (2026-09-16)

The previous comment held this open because 35s was fast enough to suspect the steps had no-opped. Read the job log once the full run finished. They ran.

From [the web job](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/actions/runs/35096598266/job/104795375681):

```
Install    added 464 packages, and audited 487 packages in 17s
Test       # pass 60
Test       # fail 0
Lint       ✔ No ESLint warnings or errors
Typecheck  > tsc --noEmit
```

The 35s is accounted for: 17s of it is `npm ci` installing 464 packages, and the three suites are genuinely fast. Typecheck produces no output on success, which is why it needed checking separately rather than being inferred from a green tick — it appears in the log with `tsc --noEmit` and exits clean.

Whole run green: `web` 35s, `infra` 1m43s, `python` 15m23s.

**This card is done.** The web app now has a CI gate, it executes all three suites, and it can fail — verified by exit code locally before the push.

## What this gate is now protecting

The first change to pass through it should be [PR #353](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/pull/353), which modifies `web/lib/turn-grant.ts` — the payload builder deciding what authority a bot receives. Those tests existed and were unexecuted by any pipeline until now.
